transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, uh… I guess the main thing is people keep telling me I’m not listening. Like, not just once in a while—my supervisor at work will be standing right there talking straight to me, explaining something, and I’m looking at him like I’m hearing him, but then a minute later I realize I only caught pieces of it. Then I’m asking him to repeat himself, and it looks bad, like I don’t care or I’m ignoring him.

And it’s the same at home with my wife. She’ll tell me something directly, and I honestly think I’m paying attention, but then afterward I realize I missed half of what she said. It’s frustrating because I’m not trying to be rude. It’s like the words are coming in, but they don’t all stick, if that makes sense. That’s really what pushed me to come in.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting, restless, or having trouble sitting still, especially in situations where you're supposed to be quiet or focused?

Yeah, definitely. That’s actually one of the things people notice about me all the time. If I’m sitting in one of those safety huddles at work, you know, where everyone’s supposed to just stand or sit there and listen, my leg is going the whole time. Like bouncing nonstop. And if I’m sitting down, I’ll be messing with a pen, clicking it, turning it around in my fingers, or I’ve got my keys in my hand and I don’t even realize I’m jingling them.

Same thing at dinner, honestly. I’ll be at the table with my wife and my leg’s bouncing under the table, and she’ll be like, “Can you stop? You’re shaking everything.” Or if we’re sitting on a bench somewhere, people tell me I’m moving it because my foot keeps going. I don’t always notice I’m doing it until somebody points it out, but once they do, I realize I’ve been moving the whole time. It’s like sitting still takes effort, if that makes sense.
Do you often find yourself having trouble completing tasks or projects?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that one. I mean, everybody has stuff they don’t finish sometimes, right? If you mean like big projects where I just abandon them halfway through, I don’t know that I’ve really noticed a clear pattern like that.

At work, most things kind of have to get done because the line is moving or there’s a schedule, so it’s not like I can just walk away from it. And at home… I mean, I guess there are normal things that sit around sometimes, but I can’t say for sure it’s a major thing I’ve paid attention to. I’d have to think about what you mean exactly by “tasks or projects.”
Do you have trouble organizing your time or activities?

I’m not sure, honestly. Like, I don’t know if I’d call it “organizing my time” exactly. My days are pretty set because of work, so I kind of just go by the schedule that’s already there. If I’m supposed to be on the line or at a certain station, that sort of decides what I’m doing, so I’m not really sitting down and planning things out.

At home, I mean… I guess we have normal stuff, errands and chores and things like that, but I haven’t really thought of it as a big issue. My wife probably has a better idea of that than I do, because she pays more attention to the calendar and that kind of thing. I don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure. I guess I’d need you to explain what you mean—like being late, or forgetting plans, or not knowing what to do first? Because I’m not sure I’ve noticed a clear pattern with that.
Do you often interrupt others or blurt out answers before they've finished speaking?

Yeah… yes, I do that. Probably more than I’d like to admit. In meetings at work especially, like when the supervisor is asking something, I’ll jump in before he’s even finished the whole question. I’ll think I know where he’s going with it, and my mouth just kind of starts before I’ve really waited.

And then sometimes I realize halfway through that he hadn’t even gotten to the important part yet. Like I’m already answering the first half, and then he adds something that changes what he was asking, and I feel kind of dumb because I basically cut him off for no reason. It’s not usually me trying to be rude or take over, it’s more like the answer is sitting right there and I feel this urge to get it out before I lose it or before somebody else says something. But yeah, I do interrupt that way.
Do you have trouble waiting for your turn in conversations or activities?

Yeah, I do. Not just in conversations, but at work especially, with activities or jobs on the line. I have a hard time waiting until it’s actually my turn to step in.

Like if I see a coworker setting something up and I think they’re doing it too slow or not the way I would do it, I’ll just kind of reach in and start adjusting it, or I’ll tell them, “No, no, do it this way,” before they’ve asked me for help. And then it turns into a thing because, honestly, they’re right to get annoyed. It’s their station, their job at that moment, and I’m cutting into it like I’m in charge or like I can’t just wait and let them finish.

It’s not that I’m trying to start arguments. In my head it feels like, “I see the problem, I can fix it quick,” and then I’m already doing it before I’ve really thought about whether I should. But yeah, it causes problems. People snap at me, or I snap back, and then it becomes an argument because I didn’t wait my turn or stay out of it.
Do you think your main problem is more with paying attention to details and following through on instructions, or with controlling your impulses and activities?

I’d say it’s more the impulse side, if I’m being honest. I mean, I can have trouble with details here and there like anybody, but the thing that gets me in trouble the most is not stopping myself before I jump in.

Like at work, if I see somebody doing a setup and I think, “That’s not right,” or “I can do that faster,” I don’t always wait for them to ask or finish what they’re doing. I’ll just reach in and start fixing something, or I’ll tell them how to do it while they’re still in the middle of doing their own job. And I know how that sounds — it sounds bossy, and it probably feels disrespectful to them — but in the moment it doesn’t feel like I’m trying to take over. It feels more like my body is already moving before I’ve had time to think, “Hold on, this isn’t your station, let them handle it.”

That’s where arguments start. They’ll say, “Back off, I’ve got it,” or get mad because I’m in their space, and then I get defensive because I feel like I was just trying to help or fix it quickly. But really, the issue is I didn’t wait my turn. I cut into what they were doing without being asked. So yeah, for me it’s more controlling that urge to jump in and act than it is following instructions.
Do you think you have more trouble sitting still and being patient, or do you have more trouble with forgetting things or making careless mistakes?

Definitely more trouble with sitting still and being patient. I mean, I do make mistakes sometimes, sure, but the thing I really feel in my body is when I’m supposed to just sit there and wait.

It’s like this pressure starts building up inside me, especially in my chest and my legs. My legs feel like they need to move, and my chest gets this tight, restless feeling, like there’s energy trapped in there. And it’s not just “I’m a little bored.” It’s more like, if I don’t move or do something right now, I’m going to crawl out of my skin.

So if I’m sitting somewhere and I’m supposed to be calm, I’m usually fighting that feeling the whole time. I’m thinking about how much longer I have to stay there, or when I can get up, or what I can do with my hands or my feet. Being patient feels like holding something back physically, not just mentally.
Do you often find yourself getting easily frustrated or angry in situations?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that one. I mean, I do get annoyed like anyone does, especially if something feels like it’s dragging on or not going the way I think it should, but I don’t know if I’d say I’m angry all the time or anything like that.

When you say “easily frustrated,” I guess I’d need to think about what you mean exactly. Like, frustrated in the moment, yeah, that can happen. But I don’t know if I’ve really paid attention to it as its own thing, separate from just being impatient or wanting something to move along. Sometimes it’s hard for me to tell if I’m actually mad, or if I’m just wound up and reacting too fast.

So… I guess I’d say maybe, but I’m not sure. I haven’t really tracked it that way.
Do you think your difficulty with listening and following instructions is more because you're not paying attention or because you're too impatient to wait for the rest of the information?

I think it’s more like… I’m not waiting long enough to really take in the whole thing, if that makes sense. It’s not always that I’m staring off into space or don’t care what they’re saying. A lot of times they are talking right to me — my supervisor at work, or my wife at home — and I’m looking at them, I’m nodding, I think I’m listening.

But then a minute later I realize I only caught half of what they said. Like I’ll remember the first part, or the part that sounded most important right away, and then I’m already thinking about what I’m going to do or what I’m going to say back. Then they’ll say, “That’s not what I told you,” or “Did you even hear me?” And I’m standing there feeling stupid because I honestly thought I was listening.

That’s kind of what brought me in, really. People keep saying I’m not listening. My supervisor will give me instructions, or my wife will be explaining something, and then I have to ask them to repeat it because I missed pieces of it. I don’t mean to ignore them, but I don’t seem to stay with the information long enough to get the whole thing. So I guess it’s partly attention, but it feels tied to being too quick — like I jump ahead before they’re done.
Do you think you would be able to focus and listen better if you were doing something that really interests you?

Yeah… I mean, maybe. If it’s something I’m really into, I probably do better, at least for a while. But the thing that made me come in is that even when I’m trying to listen, and even when the person is talking directly to me, I’m still missing pieces.

Like my supervisor will be giving me instructions, and I’m looking at him, I’m nodding, I’m thinking, “Okay, I’ve got it.” Or my wife will be explaining something at home, and I’m not trying to tune her out. But then a minute later I realize I only caught half of what was said. I’ll have the first part, or some random part, but not the whole thing, and then I have to ask them to repeat it.

And that’s what people keep saying to me — “You’re not listening.” It’s frustrating because in my head I was listening. I wasn’t trying to ignore them. It’s just like the information doesn’t all stay with me long enough, or I’m already moving ahead before they’re finished. So interest might help some, but this keeps happening with regular stuff I actually need to hear.
Do you think your main issue is more with not being able to focus on what's being said or with interrupting others because you can't wait to respond?

I think it’s more that I’m not really getting all of what’s being said, even when I’m trying to. The interrupting thing can happen sometimes, I guess, but the bigger problem — the thing that actually made me come in — is people keep telling me I’m not listening.

Like my supervisor will be talking straight to me, giving me instructions, and I’m looking at him and thinking I’m following. Or my wife will be explaining something at home, and I’m not off doing something else, I’m right there. But then a minute later I realize I only caught part of it — maybe the first half, or one piece that stuck out — and then I’m asking, “Wait, can you say that again?” And that’s when they get frustrated, like, “I just told you this.”

So I don’t know if I’d call it not being able to focus exactly, because in the moment I feel like I am focusing. But somehow the whole thing doesn’t land. It’s like I’m present, but I’m not holding onto all the information. That’s the part that keeps causing problems.

Do you think your trouble with listening and following instructions is more because you're distracted and can't pay attention or because you're too impatient and can't wait for the rest of the information?

It feels like it’s more that I don’t get the whole thing, even when I’m trying to pay attention. I know I’ve kind of said this already, but that’s really the thing that brought me in — people keep telling me I’m not listening.

Like at work, my supervisor can be standing right in front of me, giving me instructions, and I’m looking at him, nodding along, thinking, “Okay, I’ve got it.” Or my wife will be talking to me at home, and I’m not trying to be rude or ignore her. But then a minute later, when I go to do whatever they said, I realize I only caught half of it. Then I have to ask, “Wait, what was that again?” or “Can you say that one more time?” And by then they’re already irritated because, from their point of view, they just told me.

So I don’t know if I’d call it distracted exactly, and I don’t know if it’s just impatience either. It’s like I’m there, I’m hearing words, but the whole message doesn’t stick. I catch part of it, and then the rest is gone or I’ve already moved past it somehow. That’s the part that keeps causing problems.
Do you think you act impulsively more often than you have trouble paying attention?

Yeah… I think the impulsive side is a big part of it too. Maybe even more obvious to other people, honestly.

At work especially, I’ll jump into what somebody else is doing before they ask me. Like if a coworker is setting up a machine or getting something lined up, I’ll see it and think, “No, no, that’s not right,” and before I’ve even really thought it through, I’m already reaching in or moving something or telling them, “Do it this way.” I don’t really wait for them to finish or ask if they want help. I just kind of cut in.

And I know that sounds like I’m trying to be bossy, but in the moment it feels more like I see the problem and I need to fix it right now. Then it turns into an argument because they’re like, “Back off, I had it,” or “Why are you touching my setup?” And they’re not wrong. I mean, it is their job, their station, and I’m just stepping into it without waiting my turn.

So, yeah, I do have the listening problem, but the impulsive thing shows up a lot in that way — jumping in, interrupting what people are doing, trying to fix or correct it before I’ve even given them a chance.
Do you find yourself acting impulsively more often when you're around other people or when you're alone?

Definitely more around other people. I mean, when I’m alone there isn’t really anyone to cut off or jump in on, you know? It’s mostly when I’m at work and somebody else is doing something and I see it happening.

Like a coworker will be setting something up, and I’ll notice what I think is a problem, and before I’ve really stopped myself, I’m already reaching in or saying, “No, do it this way.” I don’t wait for them to ask me, and I don’t really give them time to finish. In my head it feels like I’m helping or preventing a mistake, but to them it looks like I’m butting into their job.

That’s where the arguments start. They’ll say, “I had it,” or “Why are you messing with my setup?” And then I realize, yeah, I didn’t wait my turn. I just jumped in. So it’s not really something that happens alone — it’s when I’m around coworkers and I get this urge to fix or correct something right away.
Do you think your main problem is more with not being able to control your impulses or with not being able to pay attention to details?

I’d say it’s more the impulses. I mean, I do miss details sometimes, but the thing that gets me in trouble the fastest is that I don’t stop myself before I step into somebody else’s work.

Like at work, if a coworker is setting up their station or adjusting something, and I think I see a problem, I don’t just stand there and let them finish. I’ll reach in, move something, or start telling them, “No, do it this way,” even though they didn’t ask me. And in my head, in that second, it feels like I’m helping or preventing something from going wrong. But I’m not waiting my turn. I’m not giving them the chance to handle their own job.

That’s what causes the arguments. They’ll get mad and say, “Why are you touching my setup?” or “I know what I’m doing,” and then I realize I cut in again. So yeah, if I had to pick, I’d say the bigger problem is not controlling that urge to jump in and fix or correct things right away.
Do you think your main difficulty is more with controlling your impulses or with paying attention to what others are saying?

Yeah, more with controlling my impulses, I think. I mean, I do sometimes not fully take in what people are saying, but the thing that actually blows up on me is when I jump into what they’re doing before I’ve really stopped myself.

Like at work, if someone’s setting up their machine or getting their area ready, and I think I see something wrong, I’ll just cut in. I might reach over and move something or tell them, “No, do it this way,” and I’m saying it like it’s obvious and urgent, even though nobody asked me. I don’t wait for them to finish, and I don’t really give them the chance to handle it themselves.

Then they get mad, which… honestly, I understand after the fact. They’ll say, “Why are you touching my stuff?” or “I had it under control,” and then I realize I didn’t wait my turn again. In the moment it feels like I’m fixing a problem, but really I’m intruding on their job. So yeah, the bigger difficulty is stopping myself before I butt in.
Do you think your problems at work and home are more due to acting on impulse without thinking or having trouble paying attention to what's going on around you?

It’s more acting on impulse without thinking, definitely. I mean, paying attention can be part of it, I guess, but the part that actually causes problems with people is that I jump in too fast.

At work especially, if I see a coworker setting something up and I think it’s wrong, I don’t pause and think, “Okay, wait, this is their job, let them finish.” I just step in. I’ll reach over and move something, or I’ll start telling them, “No, no, do it this way,” like I’m in charge of it, even when they never asked me. And it happens so quick that sometimes I’m already doing it before I’ve really thought through how it’s going to come across.

Then, of course, they get irritated, because from their side I’m basically cutting into their work and acting like they don’t know what they’re doing. And I can see why that would make someone mad. But in the moment it feels like I’m trying to fix something before it becomes a problem, not like I’m trying to start an argument.

So yeah, I’d say the main issue is I don’t wait my turn. I see something, I react, and then afterward I’m like, “Why did I just butt in like that?”
Do you think your difficulties are more because you can't control what you're doing or because you can't focus on what you need to?

It’s more that I can’t control what I’m doing in the moment. I mean, I know I need to focus too, but the thing that causes the real trouble is I act before I stop myself.

Like I’ll see a coworker setting up their area or getting a machine ready, and if I think they’re doing it wrong, I don’t just stand back and let them finish. I’ll cut right in. I might reach over and move something, or start telling them, “No, do it like this,” even though it’s their job and they didn’t ask me. It’s like my body is already moving or my mouth is already going before I’ve thought, “Wait, don’t intrude.”

And then it turns into an argument because they feel like I’m taking over or acting like they don’t know what they’re doing. I get why they’re mad, once it’s happening or after it happens. But in that first second, I’m just reacting. I don’t wait my turn, and that’s the part I keep messing up.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're not doing something physically active?

Yeah. Very often. If I’m not doing something with my body, it’s like I can feel this pressure building up, especially in my chest and my legs. It’s hard to explain without sounding dramatic, but it’s almost like my body is telling me, “Move, do something, get up,” even if there’s no real reason to.

Sitting still is the worst. I don’t just feel bored — it feels uncomfortable, like I’m going to crawl out of my skin if I have to stay there. My legs feel like they need to bounce or I need to shift around, stand up, walk, anything. It’s not really a calm kind of waiting. It’s like this urgent feeling inside, like I’ve got to move right now.
